newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Bel-20 to see further gain before New Year.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Bel-20 to see further gain before New Year.

text.p: The Brussel leading Bel-20 share index ended higher on Friday helped by a stronger dollar and U.S. figures which showed that the U.S. economy was cooling enough to avoid an imminent U.S. interest rate rise.
Dealers expected a slight rise before the New Year, but that volumes would remain thin to moderate.
"We'll go a bit higher on the last day of trading (December 30)," said one trader.
The Bel-20 index ended up 0.79 percent at 1,893.27, with a moderate 1.3 billion francs worth of Belgian shares traded.
"We are in a very empty market right now...this is a decent level (Bel-20), I don't expect a large fall back in the coming week," said one trader.
Dealers expected volume to remain below average until the New Year because most institutional investors would still be on holiday.
Durable goods orders in the U.S. fell 1.6 percent for the November. Economists had been expecting a small 0.1 percent rise, this dispelled investors' fears about an interest rate hike.
One dealer said the end of January would see Bel-20 falls because company reports due out in January would not be able to meet the expectations of investors.
"Share prices are so high now that there is an over- expectation among investors for 1997 which company results will not be able to meet," said one trader.

Retailer Delhaize saw a heavy 78,707 volume traded after a newpaper report gave indications that 1997 would see further Delhaize market expansion, possibly into Asia. It closed up 0.27 percent at 1,885 francs.
Another retailer Colruyt gained 2.46 percent to 14,600 francs egged on by Delhaize's news and a stronger dollar.
